plan.name: Make reader charts readable
plan.summary: Deliver #665 in one plumbing pull request: ordinary, alternative, comparison and final-model SVGs show the complete chart with a short bounds/counts/no-proof caption, retain exact source labels in titles and data attributes and complete evidence in inert metadata, list each self-loop under its state, share routes for parallel arrows while keeping every label and occurrence, and soft-wrap at spaces using realistic monospace widths without shrinking text. Move the complete report into literal-safe HTML beside dashboard charts and Markdown in receipts, with closed expandable member and occurrence lists, matching drawing/report state numbers, all rules, qualifications, counts, provenance and temporal trace facts, and both comparison sources, deltas, limitations and final-source distinctions; preserve Mermaid publication semantics, JSON evidence, validation, capacity, verdicts and fingerprints. Use natural-size images in keyboard-accessible scrolling frames on every dashboard card and evidence page, keep state labels at least 10 CSS pixels at normal zoom, bind the new HTML and SVG to immutable presentation identities and invalidate obsolete caches while retaining all existing archive and recovery checks. This ratification intentionally replaces the named #608/#613 report-in-image and distinct-loop/parallel-route assertions and related #626/#648 presentation assertions with split-report coverage, retaining topology, readable geometry, literal safety and reading order; default offline tests cover the three example shapes and extend the existing pinned-TLC example test to require widths no greater than 2200 pixels for two-phase commit, log buffer and connection pool at unchanged bounds. Update SPEC.md with existing supporting decision citations and docs/statecharts.md, docs/dashboard.md and docs/gate.md for the split, API, sizing and rollout; the merger records a decision refining D-0347, D-0349 and D-0353, runs the pinned-TLC example check when Docker is unavailable to the builder, and deploys the dashboard only after main CI publishes receipts from the new renderer, with applicable real Python and TLAPS PR checks still required.

tests.name: TestReader665CompactExampleShapes
tests.says: The three example-shaped layout fixtures fit within 2200 pixels at a readable font size, with every state, initial, labeled arrow and complete result retained.

tests.name: TestReader665ReportDoesNotSizeTheImage
tests.says: Report-only text does not change chart dimensions or appear as drawn report text, but survives exactly in inert metadata.

tests.name: TestReader665WrapsLabelsAndCompactsLoops
tests.says: Long labels wrap at spaces without losing exact text, and self-loop lists do not spread states horizontally.

tests.name: TestReader665ComparisonSplit
tests.says: Comparison SVGs retain both charts, their annotations and full comparison metadata without drawing the detailed report.

tests.name: TestReader665ReceiptReportIsCompleteAndCollapsed
tests.says: Receipt Markdown presents the complete report with closed member and occurrence details, while reader JSON and verification identity remain unchanged.

tests.name: TestReader665DashboardReportAndNaturalSize
tests.says: A receipt archive produces a script-free evidence page with a readable HTML report and a natural-size chart in a keyboard-accessible scrolling frame, preserved on restart.

tests.name: TestReader665AllEvidencePagesUseTheSplit
tests.says: Proposal comparisons and unratified alternatives show complete HTML reports beside natural-size charts, retaining their source qualifications.

tests.name: TestReader665CardsDoNotShrinkCharts
tests.says: The shared card renderer uses a keyboard-accessible scrolling frame and natural image dimensions instead of fitting a wide SVG to a narrow card.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and eight acceptance tests covering compact charts, separate reports, and readable dashboard images. The plan check passed, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
